### 4.1 Hypotheses
A1–A9 are **hypotheses (Hyp) of the generic results** about a pair (O′, 𝓗′), where 𝓗′ is a frame and O′ an observation on 𝓗′. Lem 4.0a shows that the base pair (O, 𝓗) satisfies all of them except A6, which is a parameter condition. They are **pairwise independent**: §4.4 gives, for each one, a countermodel that violates it and satisfies all the others.

| | Hypothesis | Kind | Motivation (base) |
|---|---|
| **A1** | O′ does not depend on σ over 𝓗′ | observation | O4: B07, D04, F06 |
| **A2** | O′ does not depend on f over 𝓗′ | observation | O3: G05, H12 |
| **A3** | O′ does not depend on Ref or con over 𝓗′ | observation | O6 (con: IF, within-family; Ref: modelling choice) |
| **A4** | **Invariance under fresh additions.** O′(h⁺) = O′(h) whenever h, h⁺ ∈ 𝓗′ and h⁺ is a fresh addition to h of kind (+actor), (+work) or (+act) (Def 1.7b). A4 says nothing about f, d, Ref or con of existing items | observation | O7, O8, O9 |
| **A5** | **Neutrality for σ and f.** For every h ∈ 𝓗′ and all σ*, f*: if h[σ*, f*] satisfies F1, then h[σ*, f*] ∈ 𝓗′. In other words, 𝓗′ constrains σ and f only through F1, and no frame axiom ties any other coordinate to σ or f | frame | O4: B07 (no local channel is an *independent* norm-in-force record); D04. This is a modelling choice. It is not a claim that no attestation exists anywhere (H14), or that no corpus text states a norm state (Rem 1.11a) |
| **A6** | P ≠ V | parameter | otherwise no work can violate |
| **A7** | **Openness.** For every h ∈ 𝓗′, every fresh addition h⁺ to h of any of the four kinds that satisfies F1 is in 𝓗′. The frame thus admits actors, work events and prepared issue acts that no record references, and it does not constrain which items records reference | frame | H11; F08; F11; O9 |
| **A8** | O′ does not depend on d over 𝓗′ | observation | O2: A07, F08 |
| **A9** | **No c–con tie (neutrality for con and d).** For every h ∈ 𝓗′, every history obtained from h by changing only con, or only d, that satisfies F2 is in 𝓗′. In particular no frame axiom ties the text c (or any other coordinate) to con | frame | O6; IF's candidate concept (Conj 5.5) |

Where the hypotheses are used:
- Prop 4.1(i): A1, A2, A5;
- 4.1(i′): A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A7;
- 4.1(ii): A1, A2, A5, A6;
- 4.1(iii): A1, A2, A4, A5, A7;
- Lem 5.2: A3, A8, A9, and also A1, A2, A5 for its H-D cases.

**Lem 4.0a (the base pair satisfies the hypotheses).** (O, 𝓗) satisfies A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A7, A8 and A9. A6 is a condition on the parameters only.


**Lem 4.0b (joint non-dependence on σ and f).** Assume A1, A2 and A5. Let h ∈ 𝓗′, and let σ*, f* be such that h[σ*, f*] satisfies F1. Then h[σ*, f*] ∈ 𝓗′ and O′(h[σ*, f*]) = O′(h).


Separate non-dependence on σ and on f thus gives joint non-dependence, through histories that stay in the frame.

### 4.2 Statement
**Prop 4.1 (D1; generic).** Let 𝓗′ be a frame and O′ an observation on 𝓗′.
- **(i) Core.** Assume A1, A2 and A5. For every h ∈ R_B′ there is h* ∈ H-D′ ∩ H-B′ with h* ≈_{σ, f} h and O′(h*) = O′(h). Hence
  > O′(H-D′ ∩ R_B′) = O′(H-B′) = O′(H-D′ ∩ H-B′) = O′(R_B′).
- **(i′) Record clauses.** Assume A1, A2, A3, A4, A5 and A7. Then
  > O′(H-D′) = O′(H-B′) = O′(H-D′ ∩ H-B′) = {O′(h) : h ∈ 𝓗′, R_h ≠ ∅}.
- **(ii) The contrast.** Assume A1, A2, A5 and A6. Let h ∈ R_B′, and let w be a work event referenced in h. There are h_v and h_c, both ≈_{σ, f} h, with **O′(h_v) = O′(h_c) = O′(h)**, such that:
  - h_v ∈ H-D′ ∖ H-B′, σ_v is constant on T, and w **violates a norm that never changes**;
  - h_c ∈ H-D′ ∩ H-B′, and every work event conforms.
- **(iii) H5's wording, local form.** Assume A1, A2, A4, A5 and A7. Let h ∈ H-D′ ∩ R_B′, and let w violate in h. Then there is h′ ∈ H-B′ with O′(h′) = O′(h) such that:
  - h′ differs from h only in σ (and only at violation points of h), in f, and by additional prepared issue acts that no record references and no record constitutes;
  - w conforms in h′;
  - every change point of σ′ at which no act of h enters into force (in h′) with the new value is the entry into force of an added act.

**Cor 4.1b (the base case).** For (O, 𝓗):
- (i), (i′) and (iii) hold;
- (ii) holds whenever P ≠ V;
- in (i′), {O(h) : h ∈ 𝓗, R_h ≠ ∅} = {o ∈ O(𝓗) : o ≠ ∅}.


**Rem 4.1a (in words).** On any observation satisfying the hypotheses, "the work violated an unchanged norm" and "the norm state at t(w) was different" are not separated ((ii), (iii)). (iii) adds that the difference can be carried by acts that no record references, which is H5's "without a recorded act". **Only this last clause needs A7.** In a frame where every item must be referenced, the non-separation itself survives, through added acts that are referenced (CM-A7(b)).

**Lem 4.2 (robustness).** Prop 4.1(i) holds for every (O′, 𝓗′) satisfying A1, A2 and A5, and (ii) holds if A6 holds as well; neither needs A3, A4, A7 or A8. In particular, on 𝓗 they hold for O_¬σf, the observation of **every coordinate except σ and f**. O_¬σf sees Ref, con, d, Cap, k, 𝒜, E, W and all their attributes **other than f**. So (i) and (ii) hold even if the reference and mode coding were perfectly reliable.

**Cor 4.3 (separation requires dependence on σ or f).** Assume A5 for 𝓗′. If O′(H-D′ ∩ R_B′) ≠ O′(H-B′), then O′ depends, over 𝓗′, on σ or on f. In particular, on 𝓗, no observation that is a function of coordinates other than σ and f separates the classes on R_B. This includes any function of the records, their keepers, Ref, con, Cap, and the acts and work events with their attributes **other than f**.

Cor 4.3 derives **only** that a separating observation must depend on σ or f. It does **not** derive the further elements of H5 §5.2's necessary condition: independence from the norm-maker, the executor and the self-asserting ruling, and the mapping to a target at t. Those appear only in the sufficient conditions (§4.5) and in Def 4.9. O₂ in CM-A2 depends on f and does separate, as Cor 4.3 allows.

## 5. Performative ambiguity

**Def 5.1.** Let O′ be an observation on a frame 𝓗′, and 𝓒 ⊆ 𝓗′ a class. Identity of records and acts across histories is as in Def 1.7a. A pair (ρ, a) with a an act is **performatively ambiguous in 𝓒 at o** iff there are h₁, h₂ ∈ 𝓒 ∩ O′⁻¹(o) such that:
- (ρ, a) ∈ Ref in both h₁ and h₂;
- con_{h₁}(a) = ρ, so in h₁ the record *is* the act;
- con_{h₂}(a) ≠ ρ, so in h₂ the record *reports* a separate act.

A record is performatively ambiguous if some pair containing it is. This is a property of the fibre O′⁻¹(o), not of any one history.

**Lem 5.2.** Let (O′, 𝓗′) satisfy A3, A8 and **A9 (no c–con tie)**.
- For 𝓒 = 𝓗′ and 𝓒 = H-B′: every pair (ρ, a) ∈ Ref, with a an act, of every h ∈ 𝓒 is performatively ambiguous in 𝓒 at O′(h).
- If A1, A2 and A5 also hold, the same is true for 𝓒 = H-D′ and every h ∈ H-D′ ∩ R_B′, and for 𝓒 = H-D′ ∩ H-B′ and every h ∈ H-D′ ∩ H-B′.


**Rem 5.2a (what the model does and does not say).** In the model every referenced pair is ambiguous, including a record such as R-56 whose text states its own mode (A10: "a recording note marked not part of the ruling"). That is because the frame has no axiom tying c to con (A9). The relevant condition is this absence of a c–con tie, not A3. Whether real texts do fix the mode is the empirical question of Conj 5.5, which the model does not settle.

**Cor 5.3 (the R-A3 convention).** Assume the hypotheses of Lem 5.2. A coding rule that fixes the mode for a class of records, such as R-A3 "act and after-state are the same record" (G04), selects a proper subset of each fibre in which both modes occur. Within the model, that choice is therefore a **convention, not an observation**.

**Prop 5.4 (relation to D1).**
- **(a) Removing the ambiguity does not remove D1.** Let O⁺ = (O, Ref, con, d). No pair is performatively ambiguous under O⁺, because con is seen. Yet O⁺ satisfies A1 and A2, so 4.1(i) and (ii) hold for O⁺ by Lem 4.2. So, in this model, performative ambiguity is **not necessary** for non-identifiability.
- **(b) What removing it gives.** Under O⁺, d(a) = r(con(a)) is determined for every constituted act (F2). In H-D, every issue act a in force satisfies f(a) ≥ min{d(b)}, where b ranges over its effective adopters (including a itself when prep(a) = 0); this follows from D-st. If all of these adopters are constituted, recording time becomes a **lower** bound on entry into force. This is consistent with G05, which says recording time is not an *upper* bound. H-B has no such bound: take an act constituted at r = 1, with prep 0 and f = 0. The bound concerns f, which is unobserved (A2), so no separation follows.
- **(c) What the ambiguity blocks.** If (ρ, a) is performatively ambiguous in 𝓒 at o and a is an act on τ, then "ρ is independent for τ" (Def 4.9) is **false in h₁**, by its first clause. So it does not hold throughout the fibre 𝓒 ∩ O′⁻¹(o), and O′ cannot certify any such record as independent. (Independence may also fail in h₂, for example when k(ρ) = α(a). Nothing here depends on h₂.) Keeper unobservability (O7) is a **separate**, second obstacle to the same certification.


**Rem 5.4a (application to the corpus).** Within R4's model, performative ambiguity does not *explain* the non-identifiability of H-D and H-B (IF's point (ii)). It accounts for a weaker fact: **why the corpus cannot certify one of its own records as an independent observable of the kind Rem 4.9a describes.** Both performative ambiguity and D1 stem from what the observation does not see, but they rest on different unseen coordinates: con and d (with the absence of a c–con tie) for the ambiguity, and σ and f for D1. Applying this to the actual corpus presupposes that the corpus is adequately modelled by (O, 𝓗), which is a modelling choice.

**Obs IF-obs (instrument finding; exploratory parts so marked).** IF reports:
- the binary core instrument FAILS its pre-registered rule: 2 of 9 pair × field cells reach κ ≥ 0.67;
- ACT_SELF_PERFORMED fails for every pair (0.598, 0.583, 0.637);
- *exploratory, one reviewer's judgement:* the 8 opus~sonnet disagreements on ACT_SELF_PERFORMED are all class (c), "schema admits both", and each "turns on whether a register/ruling row's words *perform* the ruling or *describe* it";
- *exploratory:* the failure lies in the register and ruling rows, not in the R15–R21 evidence-matrix rows, where all coders give SP = NO.

All of this is within the Claude family, on 36 records, with no ground truth. IF's consequence is "stated, not adopted". IF is not an R3 item.

**Conj 5.5 (performative ambiguity and the coding failure). Stated as a conjecture, not established.**
> On the register and ruling records of this corpus **outside S_mode** (the sealed set of records whose text states its own mode; see the pre-registration requirement below), the text of a record does not determine whether the record constitutes the act it refers to. This is the empirical counterpart of the **absence of a c–con tie (A9)** and of Def 5.1. It is not the counterpart of A3. The failure of ACT_SELF_PERFORMED reported in IF is a consequence of this ambiguity, and not only of coder competence or of the wording of the coding scheme.

*Scope (r2, NB-5).* The conjecture does not claim that the text fails to determine the mode on S_mode. On S_mode it predicts *less* disagreement (the second expected consequence; F-c). r1 stated the conjecture for all register and ruling records, which conflicted with F-c's use of S_mode; that wording is replaced.

Obs IF-obs is consistent with the conjecture.

**Expected consequences, if true:**
- disagreement concentrates on records whose text could be either the act or its report;
- records whose text cannot itself be a norm-making act show agreement, and records whose text states its own mode (S_mode) show less disagreement than the other register and ruling records (F-c);
- any rule that raises agreement does so by stipulating the mode (Cor 5.3). Two different admissible conventions would each be reproducible, yet disagree with each other.

**Pre-registration requirement for the falsifiers.** Before any coding for F-a to F-c, the following are fixed and sealed:
- the list of record ids forming "the register and ruling records";
- the coder pairs;
- the set S_mode used by F-c, as a subset of that list;
- F-b's review protocol: the reviewers (or the rule selecting them), the reviewer instructions, and F-b's decision rule as stated below (r2, NB-4).

**It would be falsified by any of the following.**
- **(F-a)** Coders who receive only the texts, with no added mode convention, reach **IF's pre-registered reliability rule, κ ≥ 0.67 for every coder pair** on the field ACT_SELF_PERFORMED, over the sealed list of register and ruling records **outside S_mode**. Cross-family or human coders are especially relevant here; the R2 decision is still pending (F15). This would show that the text does determine the mode.
- **(F-b)** A pre-registered independent review classifies the disagreeing cells as coder deviations ("schema admits one answer") rather than "schema admits both". This would point to competence, not ambiguity. **Pre-fixed decision rule (r2, NB-4):**
  - *Cells.* Every ACT_SELF_PERFORMED cell, on a record of the sealed list outside S_mode, on which a sealed coder pair disagrees.
  - *Who reviews.* Two reviewers. Neither is a coder in any sealed pair, the author of R4, or the reviewer who made IF's exploratory disagreement anatomy. At least one is outside the Claude family or human if the R2 decision (F15) permits; if it does not, this is recorded and F-b is read as within-family. Each reviewer sees the record text, the coding schema and the two codes, but not the coder identities, and classifies without seeing the other reviewer's classification.
  - *Classes.* Each reviewer assigns every cell to (a) "schema admits one answer" (a coder deviation) or (c) "schema admits both", the two classes of IF's anatomy.
  - *Validity condition.* The two reviewers' agreement on (a)/(c) over all cells reaches κ ≥ 0.67 (IF's threshold). If κ is undefined because both reviewers assign the same single class to every cell, the condition counts as met. If the condition fails, F-b is **undecided** and counts neither for nor against Conj 5.5.
  - *Threshold.* A cell is a deviation iff both reviewers assign (a). F-b **falsifies** Conj 5.5 iff, for every sealed coder pair with at least one disagreeing cell, strictly more than half of that pair's disagreeing cells are deviations. Otherwise F-b does not falsify. If no pair has a disagreeing cell, F-b is void, and F-a bears instead.
- **(F-c)** For every coder pair, the proportion of disagreements on ACT_SELF_PERFORMED is no lower on S_mode than on the other sealed register and ruling records. S_mode is the set of records whose text states its own mode. Selecting S_mode is itself a mode judgement, so it is made once, before any coding, and not revised afterwards. R-56 (A10, a recording note marked not part of the ruling) is the only such record named in the inputs. A result of F-c is read conditional on the sealed S_mode; a later dispute about S_mode is not evidence for or against Conj 5.5. This would show that the ambiguity explanation does no work. **Power (r2, NB-5): F-c may have no power.** If the sealed S_mode is empty, F-c is void. If S_mode = {R-56}, F-c rests on a single record, and each pair's proportion on S_mode can only be 0 or 1. The inputs also do not establish that R-56 is among the 36 records IF coded. R4 therefore does not claim that F-c can falsify Conj 5.5 with any power; the conjecture's falsifiability rests on F-a and F-b.

Scope: IF is within-family, on these records, with no ground truth. Conj 5.5 says nothing about other corpora. R5 cannot test it.

## 7. R5 specification (finite-state model; exhaustive enumeration; no code here)

### 7.1 Universe U
**Parameters.**
- T = {0, 1};
- 𝒯 = {τ};
- V = {p, q} with P = {p};
- Σ = {c1, c2};
- 𝒜 = {x};
- act slots {a1, a2}, a work slot w1, and one record ρ1, which is always present. The slot names are the identifiers of Def 1.7a;
- k(ρ1) = x, fixed and not enumerated.

**Coordinates to enumerate.**

| Coordinate | Range |
|---|---|
| σ(0), σ(1) | V |
| each act slot | absent, or present with: kind ∈ {iss, adp}; d ∈ T; actor x. For iss: v ∈ V, prep ∈ {0, 1}, f ∈ {0, 1, ∞} (target τ). For adp: obj = the other slot, which must be a present iss act |
| Cap | subsets of {(x, iss), (x, adp)} |
| w1 | absent, or present with t(w1) ∈ T (target τ, executor x) |
| Ref | subsets of {(ρ1, a1), (ρ1, a2), (ρ1, w1)}, restricted to present items |
| con(s) for each present act s | {none, ρ1} |
| r(ρ1) | T |
| c(ρ1) | Σ |

**Enumeration order (R-1).** Histories are enumerated in lexicographic order of the tuple (σ(0), σ(1), slot a1, slot a2, Cap, w1, Ref, con(a1), con(a2), r(ρ1), c(ρ1)). Each component is ordered as follows:
- values: p < q;
- an act slot: absent < present. Present slots are ordered by kind (iss < adp), then d (0 < 1), then, for iss, v (p < q), prep (0 < 1) and f (0 < 1 < ∞);
- Cap: ∅ < {(x, iss)} < {(x, adp)} < {(x, iss), (x, adp)};
- w1: absent < present with t = 0 < present with t = 1;
- Ref: by the number 4·[(ρ1, a1) ∈ Ref] + 2·[(ρ1, a2) ∈ Ref] + [(ρ1, w1) ∈ Ref];
- con: none < ρ1 (only none for absent slots);
- r: 0 < 1;
- c: c1 < c2.

The **first counterexample** to a universal check is the least h in this order. For a check of the form "for all h there is h′", it is the least h for which no h′ exists. The reported witness of an existential check is the least witness.

**Frame.** Keep exactly the assignments that satisfy F1 and F2 (Def 1.8). The typing of obj is built into the ranges. This gives a few million assignments at most.

**Classes.** Implement the clauses of Def 3.1 literally, and H-D, H-B and R_B as in Def 3.2. "Differs at most in X" (≈_X) means equal on every enumerated coordinate outside X.

**Fresh additions in U.** (+act) makes an absent slot present as an iss act with prep 1, Ref unchanged and con none. (+work) makes w1 present, unreferenced. (+ref) adds a pair to Ref. (+actor) is not representable, because 𝒜 is fixed.

**Observations.**

| Name | Definition |
|---|---|
| O | (r(ρ1), c(ρ1)) |
| O₁ | (O, σ) |
| O₂ | (O, F̂⁰), with F̂⁰ = {(s, v(s), f(s)) : s a present iss slot, prep(s) = 0, f(s) ≠ ∞} |
| O₃ | (O, Ref) |
| O₃′ | (O, con) |
| O₄ | (O, presence of w1) |
| O₄′ | (O, presence and kind of a1 and a2). No attributes; in particular not f or d |
| O₈ | (O, {(s, d(s)) : s a present iss slot with prep(s) = 0}) |
| O⁺ | (O, Ref, con, d) |
| O_¬σf | every coordinate except σ and f |

Below, F̂ = {(s, v(s), f(s)) : s a present iss slot, f(s) ≠ ∞}.

**Additional observables.** "If w1 is present" is abbreviated "if w1".

| Name | Definition |
|---|---|
| Q1 | σ(t(w1)) if w1, else ⊥ |
| Q0 | σ(0) |
| Qe | p if w1, else ⊥ |
| Q2 | (σ, F̂, Cap, and the kind, prep, obj and d of each present act) |
| Q1ʙ | if w1: σ(t(w1)) when h ∈ H-B, and q when h ∉ H-B; else ⊥. It is veridical (at least) on H-B |
| Qm | if w1: σ(t(w1)) when h ∈ H-D, and q when h ∉ H-D; else ⊥. It is veridical (at least) on H-D (Lem 4.8(a)) |
| Q* | if w1: {(λ1, σ(t(w1)))} ∪ ({(λ2, σ(t(w1)))} if h ∉ H-D); else ∅ (Ex 4.5a) |
| Q′ | (σ(0), σ(1), X), where X = 1 iff some present iss slot s has f(s) = 1, (x, iss) ∈ Cap and Adopted(s, 1) (Prop 4.6 with t₁ = 0, t₂ = 1) |

(r0's Qc is dropped. It was a function of O, so its check followed trivially from K4; M-7.)

**Frame variants.**

| Name | Change |
|---|---|
| U₅ | add the axiom "c(ρ1) = c2 ⇒ σ(0) = σ(1) = q" |
| U₆ | V = P = {p} |
| U₇ | add the axiom "every present act and w1 is in Ref" |
| U₉ | add the axiom "c(ρ1) = c2 ⇒ no slot has con = ρ1" |

**Instance I7** (the CM-A7 instance in U):
- σ = (q, q);
- a1 is iss with v = q, prep 1, f = ∞, d = 0, referenced, con none;
- a2 is absent;
- w1 is present with t = 1 and is referenced;
- Cap = ∅;
- r(ρ1) and c(ρ1) are arbitrary.

For existential checks, report the least witness. For universal checks, report the first counterexample if there is one (order as in §7.1). Model-size counts may be reported, but no count is predicted. "For every o" means for every value (r, c) ∈ T × Σ of O.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Independent finite-state verification of R5-SPEC section 7 and V1B-SPEC (+SUPP).

The raw assignment space is the mixed-radix product of the enumerated coordinates
in the R-1 order, so the integer code of a history *is* its rank in R-1 order
(restricted to the frame, the order is the order of codes).  Every class is a
boolean array over the raw code space.
Usage: python3 verify.py OUTDIR
"""
import sys, json, time, hashlib
import numpy as np

T0 = time.time()
OUT = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "."

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- universe
RAD = [2, 2, 27, 27, 4, 3, 8, 2, 2, 2, 2]   # s0 s1 a1 a2 cap w ref con1 con2 r c
W = [1] * len(RAD)
for i in range(len(RAD) - 2, -1, -1):
    W[i] = W[i + 1] * RAD[i + 1]
NRAW = W[0] * RAD[0]
code = np.arange(NRAW, dtype=np.int64)


def dig(i):
    return ((code // W[i]) % RAD[i]).astype(np.int8)


s0, s1, a1i, a2i, capd, wd, refd, con1, con2, rr, cc = [dig(i) for i in range(11)]
I8 = np.int8


def slot_dec(idx):
    kind = np.where(idx == 0, 0, np.where(idx <= 24, 1, 2)).astype(I8)
    j = np.clip(idx.astype(np.int16) - 1, 0, 23)
    f = np.where(kind == 1, j % 3, 0).astype(I8)
    prep = np.where(kind == 1, (j // 3) % 2, 0).astype(I8)
    v = np.where(kind == 1, (j // 6) % 2, 0).astype(I8)
    d = np.where(kind == 1, j // 12, np.where(kind == 2, idx - 25, 0)).astype(I8)
    return kind, d, v, prep, f


k1, d1, v1, p1, f1 = slot_dec(a1i)
k2, d2, v2, p2, f2 = slot_dec(a2i)
capI = (capd & 1).astype(bool)
capA = ((capd >> 1) & 1).astype(bool)
wp = wd > 0
tw = np.where(wp, wd - 1, 0).astype(I8)
ra1 = ((refd >> 2) & 1).astype(bool)
ra2 = ((refd >> 1) & 1).astype(bool)
rw = (refd & 1).astype(bool)
Pk = (k1 > 0), (k2 > 0)
sig_tw = np.where(tw == 0, s0, s1)          # sigma(t(w1)), meaningful if wp
KIND = (k1, k2); D = (d1, d2); V = (v1, v2); PREP = (p1, p2); F = (f1, f2)
RA = (ra1, ra2); CON = (con1, con2)

# base frame: F1, F2, typing, Ref restricted to present items, con only on present acts
base = np.ones(NRAW, dtype=bool)
base &= ~((k1 == 2) & (k2 != 1))
base &= ~((k2 == 2) & (k1 != 1))
base &= ~(ra1 & (k1 == 0)) & ~(ra2 & (k2 == 0)) & ~(rw & ~wp)
for k in range(2):
    base &= ~((CON[k] == 1) & (KIND[k] == 0))
    base &= ~((CON[k] == 1) & ~RA[k])
    base &= ~((CON[k] == 1) & (D[k] != rr))
    sg = np.where(F[k] == 0, s0, s1)
    base &= ~((KIND[k] == 1) & (F[k] < 2) & (sg != V[k]))

frames = {}
frames["U"] = base
frames["U5"] = base & ~((cc == 1) & ~((s0 == 1) & (s1 == 1)))
frames["U6"] = base & (s0 == 0) & (s1 == 0) & ~((k1 == 1) & (v1 == 1)) & ~((k2 == 1) & (v2 == 1))
frames["U7"] = base & ~((k1 > 0) & ~ra1) & ~((k2 > 0) & ~ra2) & ~(wp & ~rw)
frames["U9"] = base & ~((cc == 1) & ((con1 == 1) | (con2 == 1)))
NU = int(base.sum())
print("raw", NRAW, "|U|", NU, {k: int(v.sum()) for k, v in frames.items()}, flush=True)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- clauses
change = s0 != s1


def adopted(k, t):
    o = 1 - k
    return (KIND[k] == 1) & (((PREP[k] == 0) & capA & (D[k] <= t)) | ((KIND[o] == 2) & capA & (D[o] <= t)))


ad_k_t = {(k, t): adopted(k, t) for k in range(2) for t in range(2)}

for k in range(2):

Dchg = ~change | (act_f1 & capI)
Dchg_e = ~change | act_f1
Dchg_j = Dchg & change

Bchg_gp = Bchg_g & act_f1
Bconf = ~wp | (sig_tw == 0)

def classes(reading, fr):

    Fm = frames[fr]

    RB = Fm & r["Brec"]
    HDp = Fm & r["Dchg"] & (Dstp if True else None) & Drec    # H-D+ (D-st replaced by D-st+)
    return dict(F=Fm, HD=HD, HB=HB, RB=RB, HDp=HDp)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- history <-> code
SIG = ["p", "q"]; FN = [0, 1, "inf"]


def slot_to_json(idx):
    if idx == 0:
        return None
    if idx <= 24:
        j = idx - 1
        return {"kind": "iss", "d": j // 12, "v": SIG[(j // 6) % 2], "prep": (j // 3) % 2, "f": FN[j % 3]}
    return {"kind": "adp", "d": idx - 25}


def hist(c):
    c = int(c)
    dg = [(c // W[i]) % RAD[i] for i in range(11)]
    sl = [slot_to_json(dg[2]), slot_to_json(dg[3])]
    if sl[0] and sl[0]["kind"] == "adp": sl[0]["obj"] = "a2"
    if sl[1] and sl[1]["kind"] == "adp": sl[1]["obj"] = "a1"
    cap = [n for b, n in ((1, "iss"), (2, "adp")) if dg[4] & b]
    ref = [n for b, n in ((4, "a1"), (2, "a2"), (1, "w1")) if dg[6] & b]
    return {"sigma": [SIG[dg[0]], SIG[dg[1]]], "a1": sl[0], "a2": sl[1], "Cap": cap,
            "w1": None if dg[5] == 0 else {"t": dg[5] - 1}, "Ref": ref,
            "con": {"a1": None if dg[2] == 0 else ("rho1" if dg[7] else "none"),
                    "a2": None if dg[3] == 0 else ("rho1" if dg[8] else "none")},
            "r": dg[9], "c": "c%d" % (dg[10] + 1)}


def iss(d, v, prep, f):
    return 1 + ((d * 2 + SIG.index(v)) * 2 + prep) * 3 + FN.index(f)


def enc(sigma, a1, a2, cap, w, ref, con=(0, 0), r=0, c=1):
    """a1,a2: slot idx; cap: iterable of 'iss','adp'; w: None or t; ref: iterable of a1,a2,w1; c in {1,2}"""
    cp = (1 if "iss" in cap else 0) + (2 if "adp" in cap else 0)
    rf = (4 if "a1" in ref else 0) + (2 if "a2" in ref else 0) + (1 if "w1" in ref else 0)
    ds = [SIG.index(sigma[0]), SIG.index(sigma[1]), a1, a2, cp, 0 if w is None else w + 1, rf, con[0], con[1], r, c - 1]
    return sum(x * W[i] for i, x in enumerate(ds))


def jvals(arr, dec):
    return [dec(int(x)) for x in arr]


def o_dec(o): return [o // 2, "c%d" % (o % 2 + 1)]
def sg_dec(x): return [SIG[x // 2], SIG[x % 2]]


def first(mask):
    ix = np.flatnonzero(mask)
    return int(ix[0]) if len(ix) else None


def H(c):
    return None if c is None else hist(c)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- (iii)-L
ALLOW_NEW_A2 = [0] + [iss(d, v, 1, f) for d in (0, 1) for v in SIG for f in FN]


def iii_exists(idx, cl):
    """idx: array of codes of histories with a2 absent and w1 present. Returns bool array: exists h' as in K7/(iii)-L."""
    HBm, Fm = cl["HB"], cl["F"]
    res = np.zeros(len(idx), dtype=bool)
    cs = [(idx // W[i]) % RAD[i] for i in range(11)]
    S0, S1, A1, A2, CP, WD, RF, C1, C2, R, C = cs
    TW = WD - 1
    kk1, dd1, vv1, pp1, ff1 = slot_dec(A1.astype(np.int64))
    for sv in (0, 1):
        ns0 = np.where(TW == 0, sv, S0); ns1 = np.where(TW == 1, sv, S1)
        conf = (sv == 0)
        for fnew in (0, 1, 2):
            nA1 = np.where(kk1 == 1, A1 - ff1 + fnew, A1)
            for na2 in ALLOW_NEW_A2:
                c2 = (ns0 * W[0] + ns1 * W[1] + nA1 * W[2] + na2 * W[3] + CP * W[4] + WD * W[5] + RF * W[6]
                      + C1 * W[7] + C2 * W[8] + R * W[9] + C * W[10])
                ok = HBm[c2] & Fm[c2]
                if not conf:
                    ok = ok & False
                chg = ns0 != ns1
                # change point at 1: some act of h enters into force (f') with the new value, or f(a2) = 1 (a2 added)
                a1_ok = (kk1 == 1) & (fnew == 1) & (vv1 == ns1)
                a2_ok = (na2 != 0) and slot_dec(np.array([na2]))[4][0] == 1
                ok = ok & (~chg | a1_ok | a2_ok)
                res |= ok
    return res


def in_iii_scope(cl):
    return cl["HD"] & cl["RB"] & (k2 == 0) & wp & (sig_tw == 1)


def iii_L(cl):
    sc = in_iii_scope(cl)
    idx = np.flatnonzero(sc).astype(np.int64)
    ex = iii_exists(idx, cl)
    bad = idx[~ex]
    return (len(bad) == 0), (int(bad[0]) if len(bad) else None), len(idx)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- check forms (i), (ii), (iii)
def img(obs, m):
    return np.unique(obs[m])


def form_checks(cl):
    HD, HB, RB, Fm = cl["HD"], cl["HB"], cl["RB"], cl["F"]
    DB = HD & HB
    out = {}
    # (i)-S
    ks = np.unique(key_nsf[DB])
    miss = RB & ~np.isin(key_nsf, ks)
    c = first(miss)
    out["(i)-S"] = {"holds": c is None, "least_counterexample": H(c)}
    # (i)-O
    s_a, s_b, s_c, s_d = img(Oo, HD & RB), img(Oo, HB), img(Oo, DB), img(Oo, RB)
    eq = all(np.array_equal(s_a, x) for x in (s_b, s_c, s_d))
    out["(i)-O"] = {"holds": bool(eq)}
    # (ii)
    scope = RB & rw
    hv = HD & ~HB & (s0 == s1) & wp & (sig_tw == 1)
    hc = DB & wp & (sig_tw == 0)
    okS = np.isin(key_nsf, np.unique(key_nsf[hv])) & np.isin(key_nsf, np.unique(key_nsf[hc]))
    c = first(scope & ~okS)
    out["(ii)-S"] = {"holds": c is None, "least_counterexample": H(c)}
    okO = np.isin(Oo, np.unique(Oo[hv])) & np.isin(Oo, np.unique(Oo[hc]))
    c = first(scope & ~okO)
    out["(ii)-O"] = {"holds": c is None, "least_counterexample": H(c)}
    holds, c, n = iii_L(cl)
    out["(iii)-L"] = {"holds": holds, "least_counterexample": H(c), "scope_size": n}
    return out

def _iii_exists_o4p(idx, cl):
    """(iii)-L at histories idx under O4' (observation of presence and kind of a1,a2): h' must have the same O4'
    as h, i.e. the same presence/kind of a1,a2.  With a2 absent in h this excludes every added a2."""
    HBm, Fm = cl["HB"], cl["F"]
    res = np.zeros(len(idx), dtype=bool)
    cs = [(idx // W[i]) % RAD[i] for i in range(11)]
    S0, S1, A1, A2, CP, WD, RF, C1, C2, R, C = cs
    TW = WD - 1
    kk1, dd1, vv1, pp1, ff1 = slot_dec(A1.astype(np.int64))
    for sv in (0, 1):
        ns0 = np.where(TW == 0, sv, S0); ns1 = np.where(TW == 1, sv, S1)
        for fnew in (0, 1, 2):
            nA1 = np.where(kk1 == 1, A1 - ff1 + fnew, A1)
            c2 = (ns0 * W[0] + ns1 * W[1] + nA1 * W[2] + 0 * W[3] + CP * W[4] + WD * W[5] + RF * W[6] + C1 * W[7] + C2 * W[8] + R * W[9] + C * W[10])
            ok = HBm[c2] & Fm[c2] & (sv == 0)
            chg = ns0 != ns1
            ok = ok & (~chg | ((kk1 == 1) & (fnew == 1) & (vv1 == ns1)))
            res |= ok
    return res

def decode_image(name, arr):
    if name == "O": return [o_dec(int(x)) for x in arr]
    if name == "O1": return [o_dec(int(x) // 4) + [sg_dec(int(x) % 4)] for x in arr]
    if name == "O3": return [o_dec(int(x) // 8) + [[n for b, n in ((4, "a1"), (2, "a2"), (1, "w1")) if (int(x) % 8) & b]] for x in arr]
    if name == "O4": return [o_dec(int(x) // 2) + [bool(int(x) % 2)] for x in arr]
    if name == "Cap": return [[n for b, n in ((1, "iss"), (2, "adp")) if int(x) & b] for x in arr]
    return None


def summarize(name, arr):
    if name == "Onsf":
        return {"size": int(len(arr)), "sha256_of_sorted_int64_keys": hashlib.sha256(np.asarray(arr, dtype="<i8").tobytes()).hexdigest()}
    return decode_image(name, arr)

             "iS": bool(key_nsf[c] in ksDB),

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Independent finite-state verification of R5-SPEC section 7 and V1B-SPEC (+SUPP).

The raw assignment space is the mixed-radix product of the enumerated coordinates
in the R-1 order, so the integer code of a history *is* its rank in R-1 order
(restricted to the frame, the order is the order of codes).  Every class is a
boolean array over the raw code space.
Usage: python3 verify.py OUTDIR
"""
import sys, json, time, hashlib
import numpy as np

T0 = time.time()
OUT = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "."

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- universe
RAD = [2, 2, 27, 27, 4, 3, 8, 2, 2, 2, 2]   # s0 s1 a1 a2 cap w ref con1 con2 r c
W = [1] * len(RAD)
for i in range(len(RAD) - 2, -1, -1):
    W[i] = W[i + 1] * RAD[i + 1]
NRAW = W[0] * RAD[0]
code = np.arange(NRAW, dtype=np.int64)


def dig(i):
    return ((code // W[i]) % RAD[i]).astype(np.int8)


s0, s1, a1i, a2i, capd, wd, refd, con1, con2, rr, cc = [dig(i) for i in range(11)]
I8 = np.int8


def slot_dec(idx):
    kind = np.where(idx == 0, 0, np.where(idx <= 24, 1, 2)).astype(I8)
    j = np.clip(idx.astype(np.int16) - 1, 0, 23)
    f = np.where(kind == 1, j % 3, 0).astype(I8)
    prep = np.where(kind == 1, (j // 3) % 2, 0).astype(I8)
    v = np.where(kind == 1, (j // 6) % 2, 0).astype(I8)
    d = np.where(kind == 1, j // 12, np.where(kind == 2, idx - 25, 0)).astype(I8)
    return kind, d, v, prep, f


k1, d1, v1, p1, f1 = slot_dec(a1i)
k2, d2, v2, p2, f2 = slot_dec(a2i)
capI = (capd & 1).astype(bool)
capA = ((capd >> 1) & 1).astype(bool)
wp = wd > 0
tw = np.where(wp, wd - 1, 0).astype(I8)
ra1 = ((refd >> 2) & 1).astype(bool)
ra2 = ((refd >> 1) & 1).astype(bool)
rw = (refd & 1).astype(bool)
Pk = (k1 > 0), (k2 > 0)
sig_tw = np.where(tw == 0, s0, s1)          # sigma(t(w1)), meaningful if wp
KIND = (k1, k2); D = (d1, d2); V = (v1, v2); PREP = (p1, p2); F = (f1, f2)
RA = (ra1, ra2); CON = (con1, con2)

# base frame: F1, F2, typing, Ref restricted to present items, con only on present acts
base = np.ones(NRAW, dtype=bool)
base &= ~((k1 == 2) & (k2 != 1))
base &= ~((k2 == 2) & (k1 != 1))
base &= ~(ra1 & (k1 == 0)) & ~(ra2 & (k2 == 0)) & ~(rw & ~wp)
for k in range(2):
    base &= ~((CON[k] == 1) & (KIND[k] == 0))
    base &= ~((CON[k] == 1) & ~RA[k])
    base &= ~((CON[k] == 1) & (D[k] != rr))
    sg = np.where(F[k] == 0, s0, s1)
    base &= ~((KIND[k] == 1) & (F[k] < 2) & (sg != V[k]))

frames = {}
frames["U"] = base
frames["U5"] = base & ~((cc == 1) & ~((s0 == 1) & (s1 == 1)))
frames["U6"] = base & (s0 == 0) & (s1 == 0) & ~((k1 == 1) & (v1 == 1)) & ~((k2 == 1) & (v2 == 1))
frames["U7"] = base & ~((k1 > 0) & ~ra1) & ~((k2 > 0) & ~ra2) & ~(wp & ~rw)
frames["U9"] = base & ~((cc == 1) & ((con1 == 1) | (con2 == 1)))
NU = int(base.sum())
print("raw", NRAW, "|U|", NU, {k: int(v.sum()) for k, v in frames.items()}, flush=True)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- clauses
change = s0 != s1


def adopted(k, t):
    o = 1 - k
    return (KIND[k] == 1) & (((PREP[k] == 0) & capA & (D[k] <= t)) | ((KIND[o] == 2) & capA & (D[o] <= t)))


ad_k_t = {(k, t): adopted(k, t) for k in range(2) for t in range(2)}
act_f1 = np.zeros(NRAW, dtype=bool)          # some iss s with f=1, v=sigma(1)
for k in range(2):
    act_f1 |= (KIND[k] == 1) & (F[k] == 1) & (V[k] == s1)
Dchg = ~change | (act_f1 & capI)
Dchg_e = ~change | act_f1
Dchg_j = Dchg & change
Dst = np.ones(NRAW, dtype=bool)
Dstp = np.ones(NRAW, dtype=bool)
for k in range(2):
    ad_at_f = np.where(F[k] == 0, ad_k_t[(k, 0)], ad_k_t[(k, 1)])
    Dst &= ~((KIND[k] == 1) & (F[k] < 2)) | ad_at_f
    Dstp &= ~((KIND[k] == 1) & (F[k] < 2)) | ad_at_f
    Dstp &= ~(ad_k_t[(k, 1)] | ad_k_t[(k, 0)]) | (F[k] < 2)
Drec = ra1 | ra2
Bchg = ~change | act_f1 | (wp & (tw == 0))
Bchg_g = Bchg & change & wp & (tw == 0)
Bchg_gp = Bchg_g & act_f1
Bconf = ~wp | (sig_tw == 0)
Bconf_b = wp & (sig_tw == 0)
BrecW = rw
Brec = Drec & BrecW
Brec_h = Drec & BrecW & ~((k1 > 0) & ~ra1) & ~((k2 > 0) & ~ra2) & ~(wp & ~rw)
Brec_i = (k1 > 0) | (k2 > 0)
Brec_ip = np.ones(NRAW, dtype=bool)

READINGS = {
    "R0": dict(Dchg=Dchg, Dst=Dst, Bchg=Bchg, Bconf=Bconf, Brec=Brec),
    "R-b": dict(Dchg=Dchg, Dst=Dst, Bchg=Bchg, Bconf=Bconf_b, Brec=Brec),
    "R-c": dict(Dchg=Dchg, Dst=Dst, Bchg=Bchg, Bconf=Bconf_b, Brec=Drec),
    "R-d": dict(Dchg=Dchg, Dst=Dstp, Bchg=Bchg, Bconf=Bconf, Brec=Brec),
    "R-e": dict(Dchg=Dchg_e, Dst=Dst, Bchg=Bchg, Bconf=Bconf, Brec=Brec),
    "R-f": dict(Dchg=Dchg, Dst=Dst, Bchg=Bchg, Bconf=Bconf, Brec=Drec),
    "R-g": dict(Dchg=Dchg, Dst=Dst, Bchg=Bchg_g, Bconf=Bconf, Brec=Brec),
    "R-g+": dict(Dchg=Dchg, Dst=Dst, Bchg=Bchg_gp, Bconf=Bconf, Brec=Brec),
    "R-h": dict(Dchg=Dchg, Dst=Dst, Bchg=Bchg, Bconf=Bconf, Brec=Brec_h),
    "R-i": dict(Dchg=Dchg, Dst=Dst, Bchg=Bchg, Bconf=Bconf, Brec=Brec_i),
    "R-i'": dict(Dchg=Dchg, Dst=Dst, Bchg=Bchg, Bconf=Bconf, Brec=Brec_ip),
    "R-j": dict(Dchg=Dchg_j, Dst=Dst, Bchg=Bchg, Bconf=Bconf, Brec=Brec),
}


def classes(reading, fr):
    r = READINGS[reading]
    Fm = frames[fr]
    HD = Fm & r["Dchg"] & r["Dst"] & Drec
    HB = Fm & r["Bchg"] & r["Bconf"] & r["Brec"]
    RB = Fm & r["Brec"]
    HDp = Fm & r["Dchg"] & (Dstp if True else None) & Drec    # H-D+ (D-st replaced by D-st+)
    return dict(F=Fm, HD=HD, HB=HB, RB=RB, HDp=HDp)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- keys / observations
proj_tab = np.zeros(27, dtype=np.int64)
for i in range(1, 25):
    j = i - 1
    proj_tab[i] = 1 + ((j // 12) * 2 + (j // 6) % 2) * 2 + (j // 3) % 2
proj_tab[25] = 9; proj_tab[26] = 10
pr1 = proj_tab[a1i]; pr2 = proj_tab[a2i]
key_nsf = (((((((pr1 * 11 + pr2) * 4 + capd) * 3 + wd) * 8 + refd) * 2 + con1) * 2 + con2) * 2 + rr) * 2 + cc
key_nsfc = (((((((pr1 * 11 + pr2) * 3 + wd) * 8 + refd) * 2 + con1) * 2 + con2) * 2 + rr) * 2 + cc)  # also Cap erased
Oo = (rr.astype(np.int64) * 2 + cc)


def fh0(k):
    return np.where((KIND[k] == 1) & (PREP[k] == 0) & (F[k] < 2), 1 + V[k] * 2 + F[k], 0).astype(np.int64)


def fh(k):
    return np.where((KIND[k] == 1) & (F[k] < 2), 1 + V[k] * 2 + F[k], 0).astype(np.int64)


def dc(k):
    return np.where(KIND[k] > 0, D[k] + 1, 0).astype(np.int64)


OBS = {}
OBS["O"] = Oo
OBS["O1"] = Oo * 4 + s0 * 2 + s1
OBS["O2"] = (Oo * 5 + fh0(0)) * 5 + fh0(1)
OBS["O3"] = Oo * 8 + refd
OBS["O3p"] = Oo * 4 + con1 * 2 + con2
OBS["O4"] = Oo * 2 + wp
OBS["O4p"] = (Oo * 3 + KIND[0]) * 3 + KIND[1]
OBS["O8"] = (Oo * 3 + np.where((KIND[0] == 1) & (PREP[0] == 0), D[0] + 1, 0)) * 3 + np.where((KIND[1] == 1) & (PREP[1] == 0), D[1] + 1, 0)
OBS["Oplus"] = ((((Oo * 8 + refd) * 4 + con1 * 2 + con2) * 3 + dc(0)) * 3 + dc(1))
OBS["Onsf"] = key_nsf
OBS["Cap"] = capd.astype(np.int64)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- history <-> code
SIG = ["p", "q"]; FN = [0, 1, "inf"]


def slot_to_json(idx):
    if idx == 0:
        return None
    if idx <= 24:
        j = idx - 1
        return {"kind": "iss", "d": j // 12, "v": SIG[(j // 6) % 2], "prep": (j // 3) % 2, "f": FN[j % 3]}
    return {"kind": "adp", "d": idx - 25}


def hist(c):
    c = int(c)
    dg = [(c // W[i]) % RAD[i] for i in range(11)]
    sl = [slot_to_json(dg[2]), slot_to_json(dg[3])]
    if sl[0] and sl[0]["kind"] == "adp": sl[0]["obj"] = "a2"
    if sl[1] and sl[1]["kind"] == "adp": sl[1]["obj"] = "a1"
    cap = [n for b, n in ((1, "iss"), (2, "adp")) if dg[4] & b]
    ref = [n for b, n in ((4, "a1"), (2, "a2"), (1, "w1")) if dg[6] & b]
    return {"sigma": [SIG[dg[0]], SIG[dg[1]]], "a1": sl[0], "a2": sl[1], "Cap": cap,
            "w1": None if dg[5] == 0 else {"t": dg[5] - 1}, "Ref": ref,
            "con": {"a1": None if dg[2] == 0 else ("rho1" if dg[7] else "none"),
                    "a2": None if dg[3] == 0 else ("rho1" if dg[8] else "none")},
            "r": dg[9], "c": "c%d" % (dg[10] + 1)}


def iss(d, v, prep, f):
    return 1 + ((d * 2 + SIG.index(v)) * 2 + prep) * 3 + FN.index(f)


def enc(sigma, a1, a2, cap, w, ref, con=(0, 0), r=0, c=1):
    """a1,a2: slot idx; cap: iterable of 'iss','adp'; w: None or t; ref: iterable of a1,a2,w1; c in {1,2}"""
    cp = (1 if "iss" in cap else 0) + (2 if "adp" in cap else 0)
    rf = (4 if "a1" in ref else 0) + (2 if "a2" in ref else 0) + (1 if "w1" in ref else 0)
    ds = [SIG.index(sigma[0]), SIG.index(sigma[1]), a1, a2, cp, 0 if w is None else w + 1, rf, con[0], con[1], r, c - 1]
    return sum(x * W[i] for i, x in enumerate(ds))


def jvals(arr, dec):
    return [dec(int(x)) for x in arr]


def o_dec(o): return [o // 2, "c%d" % (o % 2 + 1)]
def sg_dec(x): return [SIG[x // 2], SIG[x % 2]]


def first(mask):
    ix = np.flatnonzero(mask)
    return int(ix[0]) if len(ix) else None


def H(c):
    return None if c is None else hist(c)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- (iii)-L
ALLOW_NEW_A2 = [0] + [iss(d, v, 1, f) for d in (0, 1) for v in SIG for f in FN]


def iii_exists(idx, cl):
    """idx: array of codes of histories with a2 absent and w1 present. Returns bool array: exists h' as in K7/(iii)-L."""
    HBm, Fm = cl["HB"], cl["F"]
    res = np.zeros(len(idx), dtype=bool)
    cs = [(idx // W[i]) % RAD[i] for i in range(11)]
    S0, S1, A1, A2, CP, WD, RF, C1, C2, R, C = cs
    TW = WD - 1
    kk1, dd1, vv1, pp1, ff1 = slot_dec(A1.astype(np.int64))
    for sv in (0, 1):
        ns0 = np.where(TW == 0, sv, S0); ns1 = np.where(TW == 1, sv, S1)
        conf = (sv == 0)
        for fnew in (0, 1, 2):
            nA1 = np.where(kk1 == 1, A1 - ff1 + fnew, A1)
            for na2 in ALLOW_NEW_A2:
                c2 = (ns0 * W[0] + ns1 * W[1] + nA1 * W[2] + na2 * W[3] + CP * W[4] + WD * W[5] + RF * W[6]
                      + C1 * W[7] + C2 * W[8] + R * W[9] + C * W[10])
                ok = HBm[c2] & Fm[c2]
                if not conf:
                    ok = ok & False
                chg = ns0 != ns1
                # change point at 1: some act of h enters into force (f') with the new value, or f(a2) = 1 (a2 added)
                a1_ok = (kk1 == 1) & (fnew == 1) & (vv1 == ns1)
                a2_ok = (na2 != 0) and slot_dec(np.array([na2]))[4][0] == 1
                ok = ok & (~chg | a1_ok | a2_ok)
                res |= ok
    return res


def in_iii_scope(cl):
    return cl["HD"] & cl["RB"] & (k2 == 0) & wp & (sig_tw == 1)


def iii_L(cl):
    sc = in_iii_scope(cl)
    idx = np.flatnonzero(sc).astype(np.int64)
    ex = iii_exists(idx, cl)
    bad = idx[~ex]
    return (len(bad) == 0), (int(bad[0]) if len(bad) else None), len(idx)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- check forms (i), (ii), (iii)
def img(obs, m):
    return np.unique(obs[m])


def form_checks(cl):
    HD, HB, RB, Fm = cl["HD"], cl["HB"], cl["RB"], cl["F"]
    DB = HD & HB
    out = {}
    # (i)-S
    ks = np.unique(key_nsf[DB])
    miss = RB & ~np.isin(key_nsf, ks)
    c = first(miss)
    out["(i)-S"] = {"holds": c is None, "least_counterexample": H(c)}
    # (i)-O
    s_a, s_b, s_c, s_d = img(Oo, HD & RB), img(Oo, HB), img(Oo, DB), img(Oo, RB)
    eq = all(np.array_equal(s_a, x) for x in (s_b, s_c, s_d))
    out["(i)-O"] = {"holds": bool(eq)}
    # (ii)
    scope = RB & rw
    hv = HD & ~HB & (s0 == s1) & wp & (sig_tw == 1)
    hc = DB & wp & (sig_tw == 0)
    okS = np.isin(key_nsf, np.unique(key_nsf[hv])) & np.isin(key_nsf, np.unique(key_nsf[hc]))
    c = first(scope & ~okS)
    out["(ii)-S"] = {"holds": c is None, "least_counterexample": H(c)}
    okO = np.isin(Oo, np.unique(Oo[hv])) & np.isin(Oo, np.unique(Oo[hc]))
    c = first(scope & ~okO)
    out["(ii)-O"] = {"holds": c is None, "least_counterexample": H(c)}
    holds, c, n = iii_L(cl)
    out["(iii)-L"] = {"holds": holds, "least_counterexample": H(c), "scope_size": n}
    return out


# ================================================================== R5 CHECKS
def run_R5():
    res = {}
    U = classes("R0", "U")
    HD, HB, RB = U["HD"], U["HB"], U["RB"]
    DB = HD & HB
    allU = base

    # K1
    w = {"H-D": first(HD), "H-B": first(HB), "H-D&H-B": first(DB), "H-D\\H-B": first(HD & ~HB), "H-B\\H-D": first(HB & ~HD)}
    lem36 = bool(((HD | HB) & ~((k1 > 0) | (k2 > 0))).sum() == 0)
    c36 = first((HD | HB) & ~((k1 > 0) | (k2 > 0)))
    res["K1"] = {"result": all(v is not None for v in w.values()) and lem36,
                 "least_witness_or_counterexample": {k: H(v) for k, v in w.items()},
                 "sizes": {"H-D": int(HD.sum()), "H-B": int(HB.sum()), "H-D&H-B": int(DB.sum()), "H-D\\H-B": int((HD & ~HB).sum()),
                           "H-B\\H-D": int((HB & ~HD).sum()), "R_B": int(RB.sum())},
                 "lem36_all_have_present_act": lem36, "lem36_counterexample": H(c36)}
    # K2
    Fm = base
    c_a = first(Fm & Dchg & ~Bchg); c_b = first(Fm & Brec & ~Drec)
    w1_ = first(Fm & Bchg & ~Dchg); w2_ = first(Fm & Drec & ~Brec)
    res["K2"] = {"result": c_a is None and c_b is None and w1_ is not None and w2_ is not None,
                 "least_witness_or_counterexample": {"counterexample_D-chg=>B-chg": H(c_a), "counterexample_B-rec=>D-rec": H(c_b),

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Independent finite-state verification of R5-SPEC section 7 and V1B-SPEC (+SUPP).

The raw assignment space is the mixed-radix product of the enumerated coordinates
in the R-1 order, so the integer code of a history *is* its rank in R-1 order
(restricted to the frame, the order is the order of codes).  Every class is a
boolean array over the raw code space.
Usage: python3 verify.py OUTDIR
"""
import sys, json, time, hashlib
import numpy as np

T0 = time.time()
OUT = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "."

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- universe
RAD = [2, 2, 27, 27, 4, 3, 8, 2, 2, 2, 2]   # s0 s1 a1 a2 cap w ref con1 con2 r c
W = [1] * len(RAD)
for i in range(len(RAD) - 2, -1, -1):
    W[i] = W[i + 1] * RAD[i + 1]
NRAW = W[0] * RAD[0]
code = np.arange(NRAW, dtype=np.int64)


def dig(i):
    return ((code // W[i]) % RAD[i]).astype(np.int8)


s0, s1, a1i, a2i, capd, wd, refd, con1, con2, rr, cc = [dig(i) for i in range(11)]
I8 = np.int8


def slot_dec(idx):
    kind = np.where(idx == 0, 0, np.where(idx <= 24, 1, 2)).astype(I8)
    j = np.clip(idx.astype(np.int16) - 1, 0, 23)
    f = np.where(kind == 1, j % 3, 0).astype(I8)
    prep = np.where(kind == 1, (j // 3) % 2, 0).astype(I8)
    v = np.where(kind == 1, (j // 6) % 2, 0).astype(I8)
    d = np.where(kind == 1, j // 12, np.where(kind == 2, idx - 25, 0)).astype(I8)
    return kind, d, v, prep, f


k1, d1, v1, p1, f1 = slot_dec(a1i)
k2, d2, v2, p2, f2 = slot_dec(a2i)
capI = (capd & 1).astype(bool)
capA = ((capd >> 1) & 1).astype(bool)
wp = wd > 0
tw = np.where(wp, wd - 1, 0).astype(I8)
ra1 = ((refd >> 2) & 1).astype(bool)
ra2 = ((refd >> 1) & 1).astype(bool)
rw = (refd & 1).astype(bool)
Pk = (k1 > 0), (k2 > 0)
sig_tw = np.where(tw == 0, s0, s1)          # sigma(t(w1)), meaningful if wp
KIND = (k1, k2); D = (d1, d2); V = (v1, v2); PREP = (p1, p2); F = (f1, f2)
RA = (ra1, ra2); CON = (con1, con2)

# base frame: F1, F2, typing, Ref restricted to present items, con only on present acts
base = np.ones(NRAW, dtype=bool)
base &= ~((k1 == 2) & (k2 != 1))
base &= ~((k2 == 2) & (k1 != 1))
base &= ~(ra1 & (k1 == 0)) & ~(ra2 & (k2 == 0)) & ~(rw & ~wp)

    base &= ~((CON[k] == 1) & ~RA[k])
    base &= ~((CON[k] == 1) & (D[k] != rr))
    sg = np.where(F[k] == 0, s0, s1)
    base &= ~((KIND[k] == 1) & (F[k] < 2) & (sg != V[k]))

frames["U5"] = base & ~((cc == 1) & ~((s0 == 1) & (s1 == 1)))
frames["U6"] = base & (s0 == 0) & (s1 == 0) & ~((k1 == 1) & (v1 == 1)) & ~((k2 == 1) & (v2 == 1))
frames["U7"] = base & ~((k1 > 0) & ~ra1) & ~((k2 > 0) & ~ra2) & ~(wp & ~rw)
frames["U9"] = base & ~((cc == 1) & ((con1 == 1) | (con2 == 1)))
NU = int(base.sum())
print("raw", NRAW, "|U|", NU, {k: int(v.sum()) for k, v in frames.items()}, flush=True)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- clauses
change = s0 != s1


def adopted(k, t):
    o = 1 - k
    return (KIND[k] == 1) & (((PREP[k] == 0) & capA & (D[k] <= t)) | ((KIND[o] == 2) & capA & (D[o] <= t)))


ad_k_t = {(k, t): adopted(k, t) for k in range(2) for t in range(2)}
act_f1 = np.zeros(NRAW, dtype=bool)          # some iss s with f=1, v=sigma(1)
for k in range(2):
    act_f1 |= (KIND[k] == 1) & (F[k] == 1) & (V[k] == s1)
Dchg = ~change | (act_f1 & capI)
Dchg_e = ~change | act_f1
Dchg_j = Dchg & change
Dst = np.ones(NRAW, dtype=bool)

    Dst &= ~((KIND[k] == 1) & (F[k] < 2)) | ad_at_f
    Dstp &= ~((KIND[k] == 1) & (F[k] < 2)) | ad_at_f
    Dstp &= ~(ad_k_t[(k, 1)] | ad_k_t[(k, 0)]) | (F[k] < 2)

Bchg_gp = Bchg_g & act_f1
Bconf = ~wp | (sig_tw == 0)

BrecW = rw

Brec_h = Drec & BrecW & ~((k1 > 0) & ~ra1) & ~((k2 > 0) & ~ra2) & ~(wp & ~rw)
Brec_i = (k1 > 0) | (k2 > 0)
Brec_ip = np.ones(NRAW, dtype=bool)

    "R0": dict(Dchg=Dchg, Dst=Dst, Bchg=Bchg, Bconf=Bconf, Brec=Brec),
    "R-b": dict(Dchg=Dchg, Dst=Dst, Bchg=Bchg, Bconf=Bconf_b, Brec=Brec),
    "R-c": dict(Dchg=Dchg, Dst=Dst, Bchg=Bchg, Bconf=Bconf_b, Brec=Drec),
    "R-d": dict(Dchg=Dchg, Dst=Dstp, Bchg=Bchg, Bconf=Bconf, Brec=Brec),
    "R-e": dict(Dchg=Dchg_e, Dst=Dst, Bchg=Bchg, Bconf=Bconf, Brec=Brec),
    "R-f": dict(Dchg=Dchg, Dst=Dst, Bchg=Bchg, Bconf=Bconf, Brec=Drec),
    "R-g": dict(Dchg=Dchg, Dst=Dst, Bchg=Bchg_g, Bconf=Bconf, Brec=Brec),
    "R-g+": dict(Dchg=Dchg, Dst=Dst, Bchg=Bchg_gp, Bconf=Bconf, Brec=Brec),
    "R-h": dict(Dchg=Dchg, Dst=Dst, Bchg=Bchg, Bconf=Bconf, Brec=Brec_h),
    "R-i": dict(Dchg=Dchg, Dst=Dst, Bchg=Bchg, Bconf=Bconf, Brec=Brec_i),
    "R-i'": dict(Dchg=Dchg, Dst=Dst, Bchg=Bchg, Bconf=Bconf, Brec=Brec_ip),
    "R-j": dict(Dchg=Dchg_j, Dst=Dst, Bchg=Bchg, Bconf=Bconf, Brec=Brec),
}


def classes(reading, fr):
    r = READINGS[reading]
    Fm = frames[fr]
    HD = Fm & r["Dchg"] & r["Dst"] & Drec
    HB = Fm & r["Bchg"] & r["Bconf"] & r["Brec"]
    RB = Fm & r["Brec"]
    HDp = Fm & r["Dchg"] & (Dstp if True else None) & Drec    # H-D+ (D-st replaced by D-st+)
    return dict(F=Fm, HD=HD, HB=HB, RB=RB, HDp=HDp)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- keys / observations
proj_tab = np.zeros(27, dtype=np.int64)
for i in range(1, 25):
    j = i - 1
    proj_tab[i] = 1 + ((j // 12) * 2 + (j // 6) % 2) * 2 + (j // 3) % 2
proj_tab[25] = 9; proj_tab[26] = 10
pr1 = proj_tab[a1i]; pr2 = proj_tab[a2i]
key_nsf = (((((((pr1 * 11 + pr2) * 4 + capd) * 3 + wd) * 8 + refd) * 2 + con1) * 2 + con2) * 2 + rr) * 2 + cc
key_nsfc = (((((((pr1 * 11 + pr2) * 3 + wd) * 8 + refd) * 2 + con1) * 2 + con2) * 2 + rr) * 2 + cc)  # also Cap erased
Oo = (rr.astype(np.int64) * 2 + cc)


def fh0(k):
    return np.where((KIND[k] == 1) & (PREP[k] == 0) & (F[k] < 2), 1 + V[k] * 2 + F[k], 0).astype(np.int64)


def fh(k):
    return np.where((KIND[k] == 1) & (F[k] < 2), 1 + V[k] * 2 + F[k], 0).astype(np.int64)


def dc(k):
    return np.where(KIND[k] > 0, D[k] + 1, 0).astype(np.int64)


OBS = {}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- history <-> code
SIG = ["p", "q"]; FN = [0, 1, "inf"]


def slot_to_json(idx):
    if idx == 0:
        return None
    if idx <= 24:
        j = idx - 1
        return {"kind": "iss", "d": j // 12, "v": SIG[(j // 6) % 2], "prep": (j // 3) % 2, "f": FN[j % 3]}
    return {"kind": "adp", "d": idx - 25}


def hist(c):
    c = int(c)
    dg = [(c // W[i]) % RAD[i] for i in range(11)]
    sl = [slot_to_json(dg[2]), slot_to_json(dg[3])]
    if sl[0] and sl[0]["kind"] == "adp": sl[0]["obj"] = "a2"
    if sl[1] and sl[1]["kind"] == "adp": sl[1]["obj"] = "a1"
    cap = [n for b, n in ((1, "iss"), (2, "adp")) if dg[4] & b]
    ref = [n for b, n in ((4, "a1"), (2, "a2"), (1, "w1")) if dg[6] & b]
    return {"sigma": [SIG[dg[0]], SIG[dg[1]]], "a1": sl[0], "a2": sl[1], "Cap": cap,
            "w1": None if dg[5] == 0 else {"t": dg[5] - 1}, "Ref": ref,
            "con": {"a1": None if dg[2] == 0 else ("rho1" if dg[7] else "none"),
                    "a2": None if dg[3] == 0 else ("rho1" if dg[8] else "none")},
            "r": dg[9], "c": "c%d" % (dg[10] + 1)}


def iss(d, v, prep, f):
    return 1 + ((d * 2 + SIG.index(v)) * 2 + prep) * 3 + FN.index(f)


def enc(sigma, a1, a2, cap, w, ref, con=(0, 0), r=0, c=1):
    """a1,a2: slot idx; cap: iterable of 'iss','adp'; w: None or t; ref: iterable of a1,a2,w1; c in {1,2}"""
    cp = (1 if "iss" in cap else 0) + (2 if "adp" in cap else 0)
    rf = (4 if "a1" in ref else 0) + (2 if "a2" in ref else 0) + (1 if "w1" in ref else 0)
    ds = [SIG.index(sigma[0]), SIG.index(sigma[1]), a1, a2, cp, 0 if w is None else w + 1, rf, con[0], con[1], r, c - 1]
    return sum(x * W[i] for i, x in enumerate(ds))


def jvals(arr, dec):
    return [dec(int(x)) for x in arr]


def o_dec(o): return [o // 2, "c%d" % (o % 2 + 1)]
def sg_dec(x): return [SIG[x // 2], SIG[x % 2]]


def first(mask):
    ix = np.flatnonzero(mask)
    return int(ix[0]) if len(ix) else None


def H(c):
    return None if c is None else hist(c)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- (iii)-L
ALLOW_NEW_A2 = [0] + [iss(d, v, 1, f) for d in (0, 1) for v in SIG for f in FN]


def iii_exists(idx, cl):
    """idx: array of codes of histories with a2 absent and w1 present. Returns bool array: exists h' as in K7/(iii)-L."""
    HBm, Fm = cl["HB"], cl["F"]
    res = np.zeros(len(idx), dtype=bool)
    cs = [(idx // W[i]) % RAD[i] for i in range(11)]
    S0, S1, A1, A2, CP, WD, RF, C1, C2, R, C = cs
    TW = WD - 1
    kk1, dd1, vv1, pp1, ff1 = slot_dec(A1.astype(np.int64))
    for sv in (0, 1):
        ns0 = np.where(TW == 0, sv, S0); ns1 = np.where(TW == 1, sv, S1)
        conf = (sv == 0)
        for fnew in (0, 1, 2):
            nA1 = np.where(kk1 == 1, A1 - ff1 + fnew, A1)
            for na2 in ALLOW_NEW_A2:
                c2 = (ns0 * W[0] + ns1 * W[1] + nA1 * W[2] + na2 * W[3] + CP * W[4] + WD * W[5] + RF * W[6]
                      + C1 * W[7] + C2 * W[8] + R * W[9] + C * W[10])
                ok = HBm[c2] & Fm[c2]
                if not conf:
                    ok = ok & False
                chg = ns0 != ns1
                # change point at 1: some act of h enters into force (f') with the new value, or f(a2) = 1 (a2 added)
                a1_ok = (kk1 == 1) & (fnew == 1) & (vv1 == ns1)
                a2_ok = (na2 != 0) and slot_dec(np.array([na2]))[4][0] == 1
                ok = ok & (~chg | a1_ok | a2_ok)
                res |= ok
    return res


def in_iii_scope(cl):
    return cl["HD"] & cl["RB"] & (k2 == 0) & wp & (sig_tw == 1)


def iii_L(cl):
    sc = in_iii_scope(cl)
    idx = np.flatnonzero(sc).astype(np.int64)
    ex = iii_exists(idx, cl)
    bad = idx[~ex]
    return (len(bad) == 0), (int(bad[0]) if len(bad) else None), len(idx)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- check forms (i), (ii), (iii)
def img(obs, m):
    return np.unique(obs[m])


def form_checks(cl):
    HD, HB, RB, Fm = cl["HD"], cl["HB"], cl["RB"], cl["F"]
    DB = HD & HB
    out = {}
    # (i)-S
    ks = np.unique(key_nsf[DB])
    miss = RB & ~np.isin(key_nsf, ks)
    c = first(miss)
    out["(i)-S"] = {"holds": c is None, "least_counterexample": H(c)}
    # (i)-O
    s_a, s_b, s_c, s_d = img(Oo, HD & RB), img(Oo, HB), img(Oo, DB), img(Oo, RB)
    eq = all(np.array_equal(s_a, x) for x in (s_b, s_c, s_d))
    out["(i)-O"] = {"holds": bool(eq)}
    # (ii)
    scope = RB & rw
    hv = HD & ~HB & (s0 == s1) & wp & (sig_tw == 1)
    hc = DB & wp & (sig_tw == 0)
    okS = np.isin(key_nsf, np.unique(key_nsf[hv])) & np.isin(key_nsf, np.unique(key_nsf[hc]))
    c = first(scope & ~okS)
    out["(ii)-S"] = {"holds": c is None, "least_counterexample": H(c)}
    okO = np.isin(Oo, np.unique(Oo[hv])) & np.isin(Oo, np.unique(Oo[hc]))
    c = first(scope & ~okO)
    out["(ii)-O"] = {"holds": c is None, "least_counterexample": H(c)}
    holds, c, n = iii_L(cl)
    out["(iii)-L"] = {"holds": holds, "least_counterexample": H(c), "scope_size": n}
    return out

    # K9.7: value 1 = {(l1,p)}, 2 = {(l1,q)}, 3 = {(l1,p),(l2,p)}, 4 = {(l1,q),(l2,q)}
    a = Qimg(Qs, HD); b = Qimg(Qs, HB)
    ok = bool(np.isin(AO(2), a).all() and not np.isin(AO(2), b).any() and np.isin(AO(3), b).all() and not np.isin(AO(3), a).any())
    res["K9.7"] = {"result": ok, "least_witness_or_counterexample": None,
                   "O_Q*(H-D)_values_(1:{l1p},2:{l1q},3:{l1p,l2p},4:{l1q,l2q})": [int(x) % 100000 for x in a if int(x) // 100000 == 0],
                   "O_Q*(H-B)_values_o0": [int(x) % 100000 for x in b if int(x) // 100000 == 0]}
    # K9.8: Qp = s0*4+s1*2+X ; (p,q,0) = 0*4+1*2+0 = 2
    a = Qimg(Qp, HB); b = Qimg(Qp, HD)
    ok1 = bool(np.isin(AO(2), a).all() and not np.isin(AO(2), b).any())
    bad = np.unique(Qp[HD & (s0 != s1) & ~X])
    res["K9.8"] = {"result": ok1 and len(bad) == 0, "least_witness_or_counterexample": H(first(HB & (Qp == 2))),
                   "n_H-D_histories_with_sigma_change_and_X=0": int((HD & (s0 != s1) & ~X).sum())}

    # K10.x ambiguity machinery
    def ambig_amb(M, obs):
        """returns per slot k the array of obs values that are ambiguous for slot k in class M"""
        r = []
        for k in range(2):
            rel = M & RA[k] & (KIND[k] > 0)
            a_ = np.unique(obs[rel & (CON[k] == 1)]); n_ = np.unique(obs[rel & (CON[k] == 0)])
            r.append(np.intersect1d(a_, n_))
        return r

    def ambig_all(M, scope, obs):
        amb = ambig_amb(M, obs)
        bad = np.zeros(NRAW, dtype=bool)
        for k in range(2):
            bad |= scope & RA[k] & (KIND[k] > 0) & ~np.isin(obs, amb[k])
        return bad

    def k101(Ucl, restrict=None):
        o = OBS["O"]
        rs = {}
        pairs = [("U", Ucl["F"], Ucl["F"]), ("H-B", Ucl["HB"], Ucl["HB"]), ("H-D", Ucl["HD"], Ucl["HD"] & Ucl["RB"]),
                 ("H-D&H-B", Ucl["HD"] & Ucl["HB"], Ucl["HD"] & Ucl["HB"])]
        for nm, M, sc in pairs:
            if restrict is not None: sc = sc & restrict
            bad = ambig_all(M, sc, o)
            c = first(bad)
            rs[nm] = {"holds": c is None, "first_counterexample": H(c), "scope_size": int(sc.sum())}
        return rs
    r101 = k101(U)
    res["K10.1"] = {"result": all(v["holds"] for v in r101.values()), "least_witness_or_counterexample": next((v["first_counterexample"] for v in r101.values() if not v["holds"]), None), "per_class": r101}
    # K10.2
    op = OBS["Oplus"]
    amb_any = {}
    for nm, M in (("U", base), ("H-B", HB), ("H-D", HD), ("H-D&H-B", DB)):
        amb = ambig_amb(M, op)
        amb_any[nm] = int(sum(len(x) for x in amb))
    kk = np.unique(key_nsf[DB] * 100000000 + op[DB])
    # K4 for O+: need h* with equal key and equal O+
    comb = key_nsf * 100000000 + op
    c = first(RB & ~np.isin(comb, kk))
    res["K10.2"] = {"result": all(v == 0 for v in amb_any.values()) and c is None, "least_witness_or_counterexample": H(c),
                    "n_ambiguous_(obs,slot)_per_class": amb_any, "K4_for_O+_holds": c is None}
    # K10.3
    ca = first(base & (((con1 == 1) & (d1 != rr)) | ((con2 == 1) & (d2 != rr))))
    okb = []
    wit_b = None
    for o in range(4):
        found = False
        for k in range(2):
            m = base & RA[k] & (KIND[k] > 0) & (Oo == o)
            ds = np.unique(D[k][m])
            if len(ds) > 1: found = True
        okb.append(found)
    res["K10.3"] = {"result": ca is None and all(okb), "least_witness_or_counterexample": H(ca),
                    "(a)_holds": ca is None, "(b)_per_o": okb}
    # K10.4
    viol = np.zeros(NRAW, dtype=bool)
    for k in range(2):
        viol |= (KIND[k] == 1) & (F[k] < 2) & (PREP[k] == 0) & (CON[k] == 1) & (KIND[1 - k] != 2) & (F[k] < rr)
    cx = first(HD & viol); wb = first(HB & viol)
    res["K10.4"] = {"result": cx is None and wb is not None, "least_witness_or_counterexample": {"counterexample_in_H-D": H(cx), "H-B_violator": H(wb)}}
    # K10.5
    o8 = OBS["O8"]
    amb = ambig_amb(base, o8)
    bad = np.zeros(NRAW, dtype=bool)
    for k in range(2):
        bad |= base & RA[k] & (KIND[k] > 0) & ~np.isin(o8, amb[k])
    c = first(bad)
    ex = enc(("p", "p"), iss(0, "p", 0, "inf"), 0, [], None, ["a1"], (0, 0), 1, 1)
    exbad = bool(bad[ex]) if base[ex] else None
    res["K10.5"] = {"result": c is not None, "least_witness_or_counterexample": H(c), "example_a1_iss_prep0_d0_r1_not_ambiguous": exbad,
                    "n_unambiguous_(h,slot)_histories": int(bad.sum())}
    # K10.6
    o3p = OBS["O3p"]
    amb = ambig_amb(base, o3p)
    n_amb = int(sum(len(x) for x in amb))
    res["K10.6"] = {"result": n_amb == 0, "least_witness_or_counterexample": None, "n_ambiguous_(obs,slot)": n_amb}
    # K10.7
    U9 = classes("R0", "U9")
    bad = ambig_all(U9["F"], U9["F"] & (cc == 1), OBS["O"])
    anyref = U9["F"] & (cc == 1) & ((RA[0] & (k1 > 0)) | (RA[1] & (k2 > 0)))
    allnot = bool(((bad & anyref) == anyref).all())
    # each referenced pair not ambiguous: check per history that every referenced slot is not ambiguous
    amb = ambig_amb(U9["F"], OBS["O"])
    n_amb_c2 = sum(int(np.isin(OBS["O"][U9["F"] & (cc == 1)], a_).any()) for a_ in amb)
    r1011 = k101(U9, restrict=(cc == 0))
    res["K10.7"] = {"result": n_amb_c2 == 0 and all(v["holds"] for v in r1011.values()) and allnot,
                    "least_witness_or_counterexample": None, "c2_histories_with_ambiguous_pair": n_amb_c2,
                    "c2_all_referenced_pairs_not_ambiguous": allnot, "K10.1_in_U9_for_c1": r1011}
    # K11.1
    hw = base & wp
    code_rm = code - (wd.astype(np.int64)) * W[5] - rw.astype(np.int64) * W[6]   # remove w1 and its Ref entry
    ok_rm = bool(base[code_rm[hw]].all())
    c_rm = first(hw & ~base[np.where(hw, code_rm, 0)])
    nw = base & ~wp
    ok_add = True; c_add = None
    for t in (0, 1):
        code_add = code + (t + 1) * W[5]
        m = nw & ~base[np.where(nw, code_add, 0)]
        if m.any(): ok_add = False; c_add = c_add or first(m)
    res["K11.1"] = {"result": ok_rm and ok_add, "least_witness_or_counterexample": H(c_rm if c_rm is not None else c_add),
                    "closed_under_removing_w1_with_Ref_entry": ok_rm, "closed_under_adding_w1_unreferenced_at_any_t": ok_add}
    # K11.2
    forced_gt = first(base & ((KIND[0] == 1) & (F[0] < 2) & RA[0] & (F[0] > rr) | (KIND[1] == 1) & (F[1] < 2) & RA[1] & (F[1] > rr)))
    forced_lt = first(base & ((KIND[0] == 1) & (F[0] < 2) & RA[0] & (F[0] < rr) | (KIND[1] == 1) & (F[1] < 2) & RA[1] & (F[1] < rr)))
    res["K11.2"] = {"result": forced_gt is not None and forced_lt is not None,
                    "least_witness_or_counterexample": {"referenced_forced_f>r": H(forced_gt), "referenced_forced_f<r": H(forced_lt)}}

    # K12.1
    def depends_by_key(obs, keyarr):
        """obs depends on the erased coordinate group iff some class of keyarr (over U) has >1 obs value"""
        kk_ = keyarr[base]; oo_ = obs[base]
        order = np.lexsort((oo_, kk_))
        ks, os_ = kk_[order], oo_[order]
        same_k = ks[1:] == ks[:-1]
        diff_o = os_[1:] != os_[:-1]
        return bool((same_k & diff_o).any())
    # keys erasing one group
    def nodig(i): return code - dig(i).astype(np.int64) * W[i]
    key_sigma = code - s0.astype(np.int64) * W[0] - s1.astype(np.int64) * W[1]
    key_f = code.copy()
    for k in range(2):
        key_f = key_f - np.where(KIND[k] == 1, F[k], 0).astype(np.int64) * W[2 + k]
    key_ref = code - refd.astype(np.int64) * W[6]
    key_con = code - con1.astype(np.int64) * W[7] - con2.astype(np.int64) * W[8]
    key_d = code.copy()
    for k in range(2):
        key_d = key_d - np.where(KIND[k] == 1, D[k] * 12, np.where(KIND[k] == 2, D[k], 0)).astype(np.int64) * W[2 + k]

    def add_dep(obs):
        dep = {"act": False, "work": False}
        # (+act): slot absent -> iss prep1, Ref/con unchanged
        for k in range(2):
            m = base & (KIND[k] == 0)
            for d_ in (0, 1):
                for v_ in SIG:
                    for f_ in FN:
                        idx = iss(d_, v_, 1, f_)
                        c2 = np.where(m, code + idx * W[2 + k], 0)
                        okm = m & base[c2]
                        if (obs[okm] != obs[c2[okm]]).any(): dep["act"] = True
        m = base & ~wp
        for t in (0, 1):
            c2 = np.where(m, code + (t + 1) * W[5], 0)
            okm = m & base[c2]
            if (obs[okm] != obs[c2[okm]]).any(): dep["work"] = True
        return dep
    k121 = {}
    for nm, ob in (("O", OBS["O"]), ("O1", OBS["O1"]), ("O2", OBS["O2"]), ("O3", OBS["O3"]), ("O3'", OBS["O3p"]), ("O4", OBS["O4"]), ("O4'", OBS["O4p"]), ("O8", OBS["O8"])):
        ad = add_dep(ob)
        k121[nm] = {"sigma-only": depends_by_key(ob, key_sigma), "f-only": depends_by_key(ob, key_f), "Ref-only": depends_by_key(ob, key_ref),
                    "con-only": depends_by_key(ob, key_con), "d-only": depends_by_key(ob, key_d),
                    "(+act)": ad["act"], "(+work)": ad["work"]}
    res["K12.1"] = {"result": True, "least_witness_or_counterexample": None, "depends_on_change_group": k121,
                    "note": "result is true because a report is produced; the content is the table"}
    # K12.2
    def closure(Fm):
        r = {}
        # A5
        viol = None
        okA5 = True
        for s0n in (0, 1):
            for s1n in (0, 1):
                for fa in (0, 1, 2):
                    for fb in (0, 1, 2):
                        c2 = code - s0.astype(np.int64) * W[0] - s1.astype(np.int64) * W[1] + s0n * W[0] + s1n * W[1]
                        c2 = c2 + np.where(KIND[0] == 1, fa - F[0], 0).astype(np.int64) * W[2] + np.where(KIND[1] == 1, fb - F[1], 0).astype(np.int64) * W[3]
                        m = Fm & base[c2] & ~Fm[c2]
                        if m.any():
                            okA5 = False
                            viol = viol or first(m)
        r["A5"] = okA5
        # A7 act / work / ref
        okact = True; vact = None
        for k in range(2):
            m0 = Fm & (KIND[k] == 0)
            for d_ in (0, 1):
                for v_ in SIG:
                    for f_ in FN:
                        c2 = np.where(m0, code + iss(d_, v_, 1, f_) * W[2 + k], 0)
                        m = m0 & base[c2] & ~Fm[c2]
                        if m.any(): okact = False; vact = vact or first(m)
        r["A7_act"] = okact
        okw = True; vw = None
        m0 = Fm & ~wp
        for t in (0, 1):
            c2 = np.where(m0, code + (t + 1) * W[5], 0)
            m = m0 & base[c2] & ~Fm[c2]
            if m.any(): okw = False; vw = vw or first(m)
        r["A7_work"] = okw
        okr = True; vr = None
        for bit, present in ((4, KIND[0] > 0), (2, KIND[1] > 0), (1, wp)):
            m0 = Fm & present & ((refd & bit) == 0)
            c2 = np.where(m0, code + bit * W[6], 0)
            m = m0 & base[c2] & ~Fm[c2]
            if m.any(): okr = False; vr = vr or first(m)
        r["A7_ref"] = okr
        # A9
        ok9 = True; v9 = None
        for a_ in (0, 1):
            for b_ in (0, 1):
                c2 = code - con1.astype(np.int64) * W[7] - con2.astype(np.int64) * W[8] + a_ * W[7] + b_ * W[8]
                m = Fm & base[c2] & ~Fm[c2]
                if m.any(): ok9 = False; v9 = v9 or first(m)
        for da in (0, 1):
            for db in (0, 1):
                c2 = code.copy()
                c2 = c2 + np.where(KIND[0] == 1, (da - D[0]) * 12, np.where(KIND[0] == 2, da - D[0], 0)).astype(np.int64) * W[2]
                c2 = c2 + np.where(KIND[1] == 1, (db - D[1]) * 12, np.where(KIND[1] == 2, db - D[1], 0)).astype(np.int64) * W[3]
                m = Fm & base[c2] & ~Fm[c2]
                if m.any(): ok9 = False; v9 = v9 or first(m)
        r["A9"] = ok9
        r["failed"] = [k for k in ("A5", "A7_act", "A7_work", "A7_ref", "A9") if not r[k]]
        r["witness_h_(an_h_in_frame_whose_admissible_change_leaves_the_frame)"] = {"A5": H(viol), "A7_act": H(vact), "A7_work": H(vw), "A7_ref": H(vr), "A9": H(v9)}
        return r
    k122 = {nm: closure(frames[nm]) for nm in ("U", "U5", "U7", "U9")}
    res["K12.2"] = {"result": True, "least_witness_or_counterexample": None, "closure": k122,
                    "failed_properties": {nm: v["failed"] for nm, v in k122.items()}}
    return res


def _iii_exists_o4p(idx, cl):
    """(iii)-L at histories idx under O4' (observation of presence and kind of a1,a2): h' must have the same O4'
    as h, i.e. the same presence/kind of a1,a2.  With a2 absent in h this excludes every added a2."""
    HBm, Fm = cl["HB"], cl["F"]
    res = np.zeros(len(idx), dtype=bool)
    cs = [(idx // W[i]) % RAD[i] for i in range(11)]
    S0, S1, A1, A2, CP, WD, RF, C1, C2, R, C = cs
    TW = WD - 1
    kk1, dd1, vv1, pp1, ff1 = slot_dec(A1.astype(np.int64))
    for sv in (0, 1):
        ns0 = np.where(TW == 0, sv, S0); ns1 = np.where(TW == 1, sv, S1)
        for fnew in (0, 1, 2):
            nA1 = np.where(kk1 == 1, A1 - ff1 + fnew, A1)
            c2 = (ns0 * W[0] + ns1 * W[1] + nA1 * W[2] + 0 * W[3] + CP * W[4] + WD * W[5] + RF * W[6] + C1 * W[7] + C2 * W[8] + R * W[9] + C * W[10])
            ok = HBm[c2] & Fm[c2] & (sv == 0)
            chg = ns0 != ns1
            ok = ok & (~chg | ((kk1 == 1) & (fnew == 1) & (vv1 == ns1)))
            res |= ok
    return res


# ================================================================== V1B
def decode_image(name, arr):
    if name == "O": return [o_dec(int(x)) for x in arr]
    if name == "O1": return [o_dec(int(x) // 4) + [sg_dec(int(x) % 4)] for x in arr]
    if name == "O3": return [o_dec(int(x) // 8) + [[n for b, n in ((4, "a1"), (2, "a2"), (1, "w1")) if (int(x) % 8) & b]] for x in arr]
    if name == "O4": return [o_dec(int(x) // 2) + [bool(int(x) % 2)] for x in arr]
    if name == "Cap": return [[n for b, n in ((1, "iss"), (2, "adp")) if int(x) & b] for x in arr]
    return None


def summarize(name, arr):
    if name == "Onsf":
        return {"size": int(len(arr)), "sha256_of_sorted_int64_keys": hashlib.sha256(np.asarray(arr, dtype="<i8").tobytes()).hexdigest()}
    return decode_image(name, arr)


NAMED = {}
NAMED["H_c"] = enc(("q", "q"), iss(0, "q", 1, "inf"), 0, [], None, ["a1"], (0, 0), 0, 1)
NAMED["H_d"] = enc(("p", "p"), 0, iss(0, "q", 0, "inf"), ["adp"], 0, ["a2", "w1"], (0, 0), 0, 1)
NAMED["H_d2"] = enc(("p", "p"), iss(0, "p", 0, 0), iss(0, "q", 0, "inf"), ["adp"], 0, ["a2", "w1"], (0, 0), 0, 1)
NAMED["H_g"] = enc(("p", "q"), iss(0, "q", 0, 1), 0, ["iss", "adp"], 0, ["a1", "w1"], (0, 0), 0, 1)
NAMED["H_g'"] = enc(("p", "q"), iss(0, "q", 0, 1), 0, ["adp"], 0, ["a1", "w1"], (0, 0), 0, 1)
NAMED["I7"] = enc(("q", "q"), iss(0, "q", 1, "inf"), 0, [], 1, ["a1", "w1"], (0, 0), 0, 1)
NAMED["W7"] = enc(("q", "p"), iss(0, "q", 1, "inf"), iss(1, "p", 1, 1), [], 1, ["a1", "a2", "w1"], (0, 0), 0, 1)
NAMED["H_i"] = enc(("p", "p"), iss(0, "p", 1, "inf"), 0, [], 0, ["w1"], (0, 0), 0, 1)
NAMED["H_empty"] = enc(("p", "p"), 0, 0, [], None, [], (0, 0), 0, 1)
NAMED["H_j"] = enc(("p", "p"), 0, iss(0, "p", 0, 0), ["iss", "adp"], 0, ["a2", "w1"], (0, 0), 0, 1)
NAMED["H_g+"] = enc(("p", "q"), iss(0, "q", 1, "inf"), 0, [], 0, ["a1", "w1"], (0, 0), 0, 1)
NAMED["H_U5h"] = enc(("q", "q"), iss(0, "q", 1, "inf"), 0, [], 0, ["a1", "w1"], (0, 0), 0, 2)
NAMED["H_U5i"] = NAMED["H_U5h"]
NAMED["H_U5i_c1"] = enc(("q", "q"), iss(0, "q", 1, "inf"), 0, [], 0, ["a1", "w1"], (0, 0), 0, 1)


def named_fields(reading, fr, cl):
    out = {}
    HD, HB, RB, Fm, HDp = cl["HD"], cl["HB"], cl["RB"], cl["F"], cl["HDp"]
    DB = HD & HB
    ksDB = np.unique(key_nsf[DB]); ksDpB = np.unique(key_nsfc[HDp & HB])
    ohc = np.unique(Oo[DB & wp & (sig_tw == 0)])
    scope = in_iii_scope(cl)
    for nm, c in NAMED.items():
        f = {"in_frame": bool(Fm[c]),
             "member": {"R_B": bool(RB[c]), "H-D": bool(HD[c]), "H-B": bool(HB[c])},
             "iS": bool(key_nsf[c] in ksDB),
             "K4b": bool(key_nsfc[c] in ksDpB),
             "iiO_c": bool(Oo[c] in ohc),
             "O": o_dec(int(Oo[c]))}
        ins = bool(scope[c]) if Fm[c] else False
        f["iiiL_in_scope"] = ins
        if Fm[c] and k2[c] == 0 and wp[c]:
            # evaluate the existence of h' even when outside the scope, keep separate
            ex = bool(iii_exists(np.array([c], dtype=np.int64), cl)[0])
        else:
            ex = None
        f["iiiL"] = ex if ins else None
        f["iiiL_h'_exists_ignoring_scope"] = ex
        if nm == "H_d2":
            f["exists(H-D+, ~sigma,f H_d2)"] = bool(key_nsf[c] in np.unique(key_nsf[HDp]))
        out[nm] = f
    return out


def run_V1B():
    res = {}
    for rd in READINGS:
        res[rd] = {}
        for fr in ("U", "U5"):
            cl = classes(rd, fr)
            ent = form_checks(cl)
            HD, HB, RB = cl["HD"], cl["HB"], cl["RB"]
            DB = HD & HB
            ent["named"] = named_fields(rd, fr, cl)
            ent["sizes"] = {"frame": int(cl["F"].sum()), "H-D": int(HD.sum()), "H-B": int(HB.sum()), "R_B": int(RB.sum()),
                            "H-D&R_B": int((HD & RB).sum()), "H-D&H-B": int(DB.sum())}
            imgs = {}
            for on in ("O", "O1", "O3", "O4", "Onsf", "Cap"):
                ob = OBS[on]
                A = {"R_B": RB, "H-D": HD, "H-B": HB, "H-D&R_B": HD & RB, "H-D&H-B": DB}
                d = {"image": {k: summarize(on, img(ob, m)) for k, m in A.items()}}
                dd = {"diff(H-D&R_B,H-B)": (HD & RB, HB), "diff(R_B,H-B)": (RB, HB), "diff(R_B,H-D&H-B)": (RB, DB)}
                d["diff"] = {k: summarize(on, np.setdiff1d(img(ob, a), img(ob, b))) for k, (a, b) in dd.items()}
                imgs[on if on != "Onsf" else "O_notsigmaf"] = d
            ent["images"] = imgs
            res[rd][fr] = ent
        print("reading", rd, "done", round(time.time() - T0, 1), flush=True)
    return res


if __name__ == "__main__":
    r5 = run_R5()
    print("R5 done", round(time.time() - T0, 1), flush=True)
    out5 = {"n_frame_histories": NU, "frame_sizes": {k: int(v.sum()) for k, v in frames.items()}, "checks": r5}
    json.dump(out5, open(OUT + "/R5-RESULTS.json", "w"), indent=1)
    v1 = run_V1B()
    json.dump(v1, open(OUT + "/V1B-RESULTS.json", "w"), indent=1)
    print("total seconds", round(time.time() - T0, 1))
